Given that $R$ is the type III region shown above, 
${∭}_{R}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}V=$
question.worked_solution:
For a type III region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

We consider the region $R$ as a type III region enclosed between the back surface $y={u}_{1}(x,z)=2$ and the front surface $y={u}_{2}(x,z)=6.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14227375/assets/a03d6986874a543bc21d274433b5268444f2487aea198834d379f004a7d85e79.png)

So, the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,2\le y\le 6\}.
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I *plane* region in the $xz$-plane with the upper curve

$$
z=1-x.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14227375/assets/06e8986d493efbe696751db410f84490ba634c9f68feaa03aa0bf9d71593feb3.png)

Hence, $D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1-x\}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{2}^{6}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}[{\int }_{2}^{6}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{x}^{2}[y]_{y=2}^{y=6}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}4{x}^{2}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$
